figures_reviewed.caption: passes: the caption states what is plotted, names the arm ordering the figure shows and cites the drawing script; it is a description, not a restatement of the figure title.

rubric.contrast: passes: black tick and axis text on white; the white-arm trace in #333333 at alpha 0.7 reads clearly against white; the blue, orange and red traces all read at a glance.
rubric.data_ink: passes: five thin traces plus two marker sets on an empty field; the data occupy the panel and nothing else is drawn inside the axes.
rubric.decoration: passes: no gridlines, no background fill, no gradient, no shading, top and right spines absent.
rubric.label_collision: no text label is clipped or overlapping: the 7-entry legend sits in clear space at upper left and no label touches a trace. Data marks do collide: the slice-0 nova markers are cut in half by the left spine, and the ring and square coincide at slices 0 and 2 (see findings).
rubric.legibility: passes for the four size arms and the white arm: the arms separate into three readable bands (0.01-0.02 near 0.01 m, 0.05 near 0.06-0.13 m, 0.10 near 0.12-0.30 m with a 0.55 m spike at slice 40) and the axes carry their units. It does not fully pass on the nova overlay: the two nova marks at slices 0 and 2 are not separately distinguishable as two sequences (see finding).
rubric.table_form: passes: a 100-slice per-arm time series is not information that is naturally a table; the surrounding record carries the reduction tables for the numbers.

findings.summary: The slice-0 nova markers are clipped in half by the left spine. axes.set_xlim(0, 99) puts the slice-0 point exactly on the y-axis, and the 5 pt open markers at x=0 lose their left half to the axes boundary, so the reader sees half a ring and half a square where the figure's one cross-code column begins. The centre and its height are still readable, so the figure's message survives; offsetting the limit below 0 or nudging the marks off the spine would show them whole.

The drift (ring) and white (square) nova markers coincide at slices 0 and 2, because both sequences were measured on the same slices and the two values are about a pixel apart at this scale. The square, drawn second, sits over the ring and the pair renders as one composite mark, so a reader cannot tell the two nova sequences apart at either slice without the legend and the table. A small horizontal offset per sequence, or one marker carrying a distinguishing fill, would let both be seen.

The panel is drawn on a 6.4 x 3.6 in canvas with a 7 pt legend and 0.9 pt lines, and saved through figure.savefig rather than the repository's style save function. It therefore misses the declared 14 in canvas, 14 pt legend and 2.4-3.0 pt line weights, and the mechanical text-overlap check that the style module's save runs on every figure never sees this one — which is why the marker collisions above reached the record. The rendered PNG is still legible at its own size; the cost is that the figure reads as smaller and lighter than every other nova figure beside it.
